I've been trying to come up with stateful linters that might be useful (it's an unreleased feature, but it's already merged in core: #lean4 > Stateful linters).

One new linter that this feature enables is one that looks for variable commands that declare binders that are then never used. One might end up with these after refactors / copy-pasting files, etc., or by just over-specifying variables that one expects 'should be used later'.

These unused binders look innocent enough, (and arguably in the 'should be used later' they might be helpful to have 'uniform' naming conventions), but the fact is that the binders are re-elaborated for every command in their scope. This can be expensive for no reason, especially when a bunch of typeclass synthesis is involved.

Should we strive to avoid this situation with such a linter? I have a working prototype in #42216, which resulted in #42214 after a sweep of mathlib. For the most egregious example in that PR: removing all the unused binders in Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.Defs:

results in a 30% reduction in instructions for that module:
Nice!! Btw, are you just building locally or something? I’m finding it impractical to try out features that haven’t landed yet in Mathlib because of the instant CI failure.

Yeah, I've been building locally against a suitable mathlib4-nightly-testing and then porting the results. I just wanted to open the discussion, these PRs should be more legit (namely: the linter itself will pass CI) once mathlib ingests a toolchain with the relevant feature
(And I guess the other point is that the discussion can happen now because the sweep in #42214 does pass)
Oh yeah, I was mainly asking just so I could try out stateful linters at scale in mathlib too without having to build locally, in case there was some secret :laughing: But this is off-topic.
I think we definitely want this unused variables linter, btw. :)
